title: Ankhorage Studio Authoring
summary: Provides renderer-neutral authoring state and manifest policy for Ankhorage applications.
purpose: Keep portable application-authoring behavior reusable outside the Studio host and independent from UI, persistence, and generated-project delivery.
responsibilities: Derive edit and preview interaction state.
Update screen metadata and requirements without changing screen identity or authored UI trees.
Resolve portable authoring routes, inspector targets, node selection, and runtime-overlay policy.
boundaries: Does not own Studio host lifecycle, user interface composition, or renderer implementation.
Does not persist manifests or generate application files.
Does not own authentication, deployment, secrets, APIs, or other host-specific Studio routes.
audience: Authoring hosts that need portable manifest and selection behavior.
Applications that embed Ankhorage authoring behavior without depending on Studio.
useCases: Switch a host between edit and preview interaction modes.
Update one authored screen's metadata or declared requirements immutably.
Resolve an authoring route, inspector target, or selected tree node independent of a UI framework.

architecture.role: Standalone feature-first authoring policy library consumed by hosts through its public package facade.
invariants: Authoring policy remains independent from UI frameworks, filesystems, network transports, and Studio host composition.
Manifest updates preserve portable contracts and authored identity.
Host-owned routes and side effects stay outside the package.

limitations: The package exposes policy and transformations only; hosts provide persistence, rendering, and delivery adapters.
